ai_technology: Logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM and KNN

evidence.ai_role: Supervised models compare event discrimination with and without existing metabolic indices.
evidence.tested: Stratified 70/30 training/test split; preprocessing learned on training data, five-fold training hyperparameter tuning, recorded follow-up event labels.
evidence.unknown: Prospective clinical benefit and external transport unestablished; cohort follow-up does not make retrospective model evaluation prospective.

organization: Guangzhou University of Chinese Medicine; Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine; Heilongjiang University of Chinese Medicine; Shanxi University of Chinese Medicine

source_review.scope: Primary full manuscript: cohort definition, actual model/input/preprocessing/split Methods and reported classification Results/limitations. No prospective utility claim.

summary: In 3,092 hypertensive CHARLS participants followed for a median eight years, a preprint compared learned cardiovascular-event predictors using baseline risk factors. Adding TyG-BMI increased reported AUC from 0.593 to 0.636; logistic regression performed best, with tree-based learners adding no advantage. This is retrospective modeling of recorded follow-up outcomes, not a prospective evaluation of a frozen model. Modest discrimination, self-reported outcomes and unresolved clinical utility limit application; the conventional epidemiological association is not itself a new AI-discovered mechanism.
title: TyG-BMI adds modest discrimination in retrospective cardiovascular prediction
